questions.stem: A Japanese investor holds US-dollar-denominated bonds. To hedge the exchange-rate risk, she should most likely:

choices.B: sell USD forward
choices.C: buy USD forward

questions.explanation: Routine: (1) what is she long? USD (the bonds pay dollars). (2) The hedge is the opposite position in the derivative: short USD. (3) Short = sell → SELL USD forward (= buy JPY forward). Selling JPY forward or buying USD forward would ADD dollar exposure. The currency you sell forward is the one you are long in the cash market.
questions.kr: 루틴: (1) 무엇을 롱? USD(채권이 달러 지급). (2) 헤지 = 파생상품에서 반대 포지션: USD 숏. (3) 숏 = 매도 → USD 선도 '매도'(= JPY 선도 매수). JPY 선도 매도나 USD 선도 매수는 달러 노출을 '추가'. 선도로 파는 통화 = 현물에서 롱인 통화.

questions.stem: A trader sold EUR 50m forward at USD/EUR 1.3100. Two days before settlement the spot rate is 1.2950 and the trader rolls the position with an FX swap. The settlement-day cash flow is closest to:

choices.B: USD 750,000 paid
choices.C: zero, since the euro amounts net

questions.explanation: Rolling = buy EUR 50m spot (delivers against the EUR sold forward, so the EUR nets to zero) + a new forward. The USD legs don't net: sold at 1.3100, bought at 1.2950 → EUR 50m × (1.3100 − 1.2950) = USD 750,000 RECEIVED. Short EUR, euro fell → profit. The price currency carries the mark-to-market; only the quantity currency nets.
questions.kr: 롤 = EUR 50m 현물 매수(선도 매도분과 상계되어 EUR는 0) + 새 선도. USD 쪽은 상계 안 됨: 1.3100에 팔고 1.2950에 삼 → 50m × 0.015 = USD 750,000 '수취'. EUR 숏인데 유로 하락 → 이익. 가격통화가 시가평가 손익을, 수량통화만 상계.

questions.stem: Compared with OTC forward contracts, exchange-traded currency futures most likely have:

choices.B: greater counterparty risk
choices.C: daily mark-to-market with collateral

questions.explanation: Futures: exchange-traded (CME IMM), FIXED amounts and dates, collateral posted and marked to market daily, minimal counterparty risk because the exchange stands between the parties — less flexible, safer. Forwards: any size/date, no collateral, counterparty risk present.
questions.kr: 선물: 거래소(CME IMM), 금액·만기 '고정', 증거금 + 일일 시가평가, 거래소가 중간에 서서 거래상대방 위험 최소 — 유연성은 낮고 안전. 선도: 금액·날짜 자유, 증거금 없음, 거래상대방 위험 존재.

questions.stem: Spot transactions most likely account for:

choices.A: the majority of daily FX turnover
choices.B: a minority of daily FX turnover
choices.C: all transactions settling within T + 2 in Canada

questions.explanation: Spot (T + 2; CAD vs USD T + 1) is the rate on the news but a MINORITY of daily turnover — outright forwards, FX swaps (the largest, from constant rolling) and options make up the rest. Choice C garbles the CAD exception.
questions.kr: 현물(T+2; CAD-USD는 T+1)은 뉴스에 나오는 환율이지만 일일 거래량의 '소수' — 선도, FX 스왑(롤링 때문에 최대), 옵션이 나머지. C는 CAD 예외를 뒤섞은 것.

questions.stem: A UK firm will receive EUR 10m in six months and has not hedged. Its exchange-rate risk arises from uncertainty over:

choices.B: the GBP/EUR spot rate in six months
choices.C: the GBP/EUR forward rate in six months

questions.explanation: Unhedged, the firm will convert at whatever SPOT rate prevails in six months — that is the unknown. Today's forward is a quoted, known price (and the hedge it declined); the forward rate six months from now is irrelevant because the firm won't be entering a forward then. Risk lives in the future spot; forwards are the known hedge.
questions.kr: 헤지하지 않으면 6개월 뒤의 '현물' 환율로 환전 — 그것이 미지수. 오늘의 선도환율은 고시된 '알려진' 가격(거절한 헤지 수단); 6개월 뒤의 선도환율은 그때 선도계약을 맺지 않으므로 무관. 위험은 미래 현물에, 선도는 알려진 헤지.

questions.stem: A eurozone investor converts EUR to CHF spot at EUR/CHF 0.9200 (EUR per CHF), buys a one-year risk-free CHF zero yielding 1.0%, and sells CHF forward at EUR/CHF 0.9300. Her EUR return is closest to:
questions.explanation: EUR 1 → CHF 1/0.92 = 1.0870; × 1.01 = 1.0978 CHF; × 0.93 = EUR 1.0210 → 2.1%. Shortcut: (F/S)(1 + i_f) − 1 = (0.93/0.92)(1.01) − 1 = 2.1%. The forward is ABOVE spot, so the CHF is sold back at a premium that adds ~1.1% on top of the 1.0% CHF rate. Choice A ignores the forward premium; C has the premium sign reversed.

questions.concept: Hedged zero held to maturity = risk free
questions.stem: A one-year, risk-free, zero-coupon foreign bond held to maturity with the proceeds sold forward at inception is most likely exposed to:

choices.B: exchange rate risk only
choices.C: neither interest rate nor exchange rate risk

questions.explanation: Tick each risk: default — none (risk-free issuer); reinvestment — none (zero coupon); interest rate — none (held to its one-year maturity, matures at par whatever rates do); FX — none (the forward fixes the conversion). All four switched off → risk free. 'Bonds carry rate risk' is true in general but the clause 'zero coupon, held to maturity' turns it off.
questions.kr: 위험별 점검: 부도 — 없음(무위험 발행자); 재투자 — 없음(무이표); 금리 — 없음(1년 만기까지 보유, 액면 상환); 환 — 없음(선도로 고정). 넷 다 꺼짐 → 무위험. '채권은 금리위험'은 일반론이고 '무이표·만기보유' 조건이 그것을 끈다.

questions.stem: Exports are 45% of total trade. ε_X = 0.5, ε_M = 0.8. Following a depreciation, the trade balance will most likely:

choices.B: worsen, since ε_M < 1
choices.C: worsen, since the condition equals −0.115

questions.explanation: ω_X·ε_X + ω_M·(ε_M − 1) = 0.45 × 0.5 + 0.55 × (0.8 − 1) = 0.225 − 0.110 = +0.115 > 0 → improves. ε_M < 1 alone does NOT mean worsening — the negative import term is outweighed by the export term. The import term uses (ε_M − 1), not ε_M.

questions.stem: Exports are 30% of total trade. ε_X = 0.4, ε_M = 0.6. The generalized Marshall–Lerner condition is closest to:
questions.explanation: 0.30 × 0.4 + 0.70 × (0.6 − 1) = 0.12 − 0.28 = −0.16 < 0 → depreciation would WORSEN the balance. Choice C (0.54) forgets the −1 in the import term (0.12 + 0.42). With a large deficit (ω_M = 0.7) the inelastic import demand dominates.
questions.kr: 0.30 × 0.4 + 0.70 × (0.6 − 1) = 0.12 − 0.28 = −0.16 < 0 → 통화 약세가 무역수지를 '악화'. C(0.54)는 수입항의 −1을 빼먹은 값. 적자가 크면(ω_M = 0.7) 비탄력적 수입수요가 지배.

questions.stem: Following a depreciation, import expenditure in domestic currency will decline only if:

choices.B: ε_M > 1
choices.C: ε_X + ε_M > 1

questions.explanation: Imports are billed in foreign currency, so depreciation raises their domestic price (spending ↑) while cutting quantity (spending ↓). Net %Δ spending = (1 − ε_M) × %ΔP → falls only if ε_M > 1. Exports have no such price effect (billed in domestic currency). C is the classic Marshall–Lerner for balanced trade, a different question.
questions.kr: 수입은 외화 표시라 통화 약세가 국내가격을 올림(지출↑)과 동시에 수량을 줄임(지출↓). 순 지출 변화 = (1 − ε_M) × %ΔP → ε_M > 1일 때만 감소. 수출은 자국통화 표시라 가격효과 없음. C는 균형무역의 고전적 마셜–러너 조건으로 다른 질문.

questions.stem: The J-curve effect is best explained by:

choices.A: long-run elasticities failing the Marshall–Lerner condition
choices.B: pre-existing contracts and lower short-run elasticities
choices.C: exports being billed in foreign currency

questions.explanation: Worse before better: (1) contracts already priced in foreign currency cost more domestic currency after the depreciation until new orders are placed; (2) short-run elasticities may fail Marshall–Lerner while long-run ones satisfy it. If LONG-run elasticities failed (A) there would be no eventual improvement — no J. Exports are assumed billed in DOMESTIC currency.
questions.kr: 먼저 악화, 나중 개선: (1) 외화로 이미 계약된 수입은 새 주문 전까지 자국통화로 더 비싸짐; (2) 단기 탄력성은 마셜–러너를 충족 못 해도 장기 탄력성은 충족. '장기' 탄력성이 실패하면(A) 개선 자체가 없어 J가 안 됨. 수출은 자국통화 표시 가정.

questions.stem: In the curriculum's Exhibit 1 (10% depreciation, ε_M = 0.65), import expenditure rose after the depreciation most likely because:

choices.B: import demand was inelastic, so the price effect outweighed the quantity effect
choices.C: exports were billed in domestic currency

questions.explanation: Import quantity FELL 6.5%, but the domestic-currency price rose 10%; with ε_M = 0.65 < 1 the price effect dominates → spending +3.5% (= 10% × (1 − 0.65)) → +€21m. The balance still improved because exports rose €30m. Export billing (C) explains the export term, not import spending.
questions.kr: 수입 수량은 6.5% '감소'했지만 자국통화 가격이 10% 상승; ε_M = 0.65 < 1이라 가격효과 우세 → 지출 +3.5%(= 10% × (1 − 0.65)) → +€21m. 수출이 €30m 늘어 수지는 개선. 수출 표시통화(C)는 수출항의 설명.

questions.stem: A country runs a trade deficit. All else equal, which change would most likely reduce the deficit?

choices.B: an increase in the government budget deficit
choices.C: an increase in private saving

questions.explanation: X − M = (S − I) + (T − G). A deficit is a negative left side; to shrink it the right side must RISE: S ↑, I ↓, or (T − G) ↑. Higher investment lowers (S − I); a bigger budget deficit lowers (T − G) — both widen the trade deficit. Write the identity, sign each term, then read the stem.
questions.kr: X − M = (S − I) + (T − G). 적자 = 좌변 음수; 줄이려면 우변이 '올라야': S ↑, I ↓, (T − G) ↑. 투자 증가는 (S − I)를 낮추고, 재정적자 확대는 (T − G)를 낮춤 — 둘 다 무역적자 확대. 항등식을 쓰고 부호를 매긴 뒤 지문을 읽는다.

questions.stem: A country runs a trade surplus. Which change would most likely increase the surplus?

choices.B: a decrease in private investment
choices.C: a decrease in private saving

questions.explanation: X − M = (S − I) + (T − G). To GROW the surplus the right side must rise: S ↑, I ↓, or (T − G) ↑. Lower investment raises (S − I) → surplus grows. A tax cut lowers (T − G) and lower saving lowers (S − I) — both shrink it. Same identity as the deficit question, opposite direction.
questions.kr: X − M = (S − I) + (T − G). 흑자를 '키우려면' 우변 상승: S ↑, I ↓, (T − G) ↑. 투자 감소는 (S − I)를 올려 흑자 확대. 감세는 (T − G)를, 저축 감소는 (S − I)를 낮춤 — 둘 다 축소. 적자 문제와 같은 항등식, 반대 방향.

questions.stem: An economy at full employment depreciates its currency. According to the absorption approach, the trade balance will most likely:

choices.B: improve only if domestic expenditure declines
choices.C: improve because output rises

questions.explanation: At full employment output cannot rise, so trade balance = income − absorption improves ONLY if expenditure falls. Otherwise the extra demand pushes prices up until the stimulus is negated and the balance reverts. 'Output rises' is the excess-capacity case; 'permanent' contradicts the temporary wealth-effect conclusion.
questions.kr: 완전고용에서는 산출이 못 늘므로 무역수지 = 소득 − 흡수(지출)는 지출이 줄 때만 개선. 아니면 초과수요가 물가를 올려 자극이 상쇄되고 수지는 원위치. '산출 증가'는 유휴설비 경우, '영구적'은 일시적 부(富) 효과 결론과 모순.

questions.stem: The improvement in the trade balance produced by the wealth effect of a depreciation is most likely:

choices.B: temporary, reversing as real wealth is rebuilt
choices.C: larger the closer the economy is to full employment

questions.explanation: A weaker currency lowers the real value of domestic assets → households cut spending and save more → balance improves — but as real wealth is rebuilt the saving response reverses, so the gain is TEMPORARY. A lasting correction needs a change in saving/expenditure behavior (fiscal balance ↑, real rates ↑). Proximity to full employment makes depreciation LESS effective, not more.
questions.kr: 통화 약세 → 자국 자산의 실질가치↓ → 가계가 지출 줄이고 저축↑ → 수지 개선 — 그러나 실질 부가 회복되면 저축 반응이 되돌아가 '일시적'. 지속적 교정은 저축·지출 행태 변화(재정수지↑, 실질금리↑) 필요. 완전고용에 가까울수록 통화 약세는 '덜' 효과적.

questions.stem: An AUD-based investor holding HKD bonds without a hedge faces exchange-rate risk that is determined by uncertainty over:

choices.B: the AUD/HKD spot rate one year from now
choices.C: the AUD/HKD forward rate one year from now

questions.explanation: Unhedged, she converts at the future SPOT rate — the only unknown. Today's forward is a quoted price (known with certainty); next year's forward is irrelevant because she won't be entering a forward then. 'Forward' is the sophisticated-sounding lure.
questions.kr: 헤지 없이는 미래 '현물' 환율로 환전 — 유일한 미지수. 오늘의 선도는 고시된 가격(확실히 알려짐); 1년 뒤 선도는 그때 선도계약을 맺지 않으므로 무관. 'forward'가 그럴듯한 유인.

questions.concept: Ex1 Q2 — sell forward what you're long
questions.stem: To reduce the exchange-rate risk of her HKD bond holding, the AUD-based investor should most likely:

choices.B: sell AUD forward
choices.C: sell HKD forward

questions.explanation: Long HKD in the cash market → short HKD in the derivative → SELL HKD forward (= buy AUD forward). Selling AUD forward is the same as buying HKD forward — it doubles the HKD exposure. Right instrument, wrong currency is the standard polarity miss here.
questions.kr: 현물에서 HKD 롱 → 파생상품에서 HKD 숏 → HKD 선도 '매도'(= AUD 선도 매수). AUD 선도 매도 = HKD 선도 매수 → HKD 노출이 두 배. 상품은 맞고 통화가 틀리는 것이 전형적 극성 오답.

questions.concept: Ex1 Q3 — hedged zero = risk free
questions.stem: The adviser's strategy: convert AUD to HKD spot, buy a one-year risk-free HKD zero-coupon bond, and sell the HKD proceeds forward for AUD. The investment is most likely:

choices.B: exposed to interest rate risk
choices.C: exposed to exchange rate risk

questions.explanation: Default risk: none (risk-free issuer). Reinvestment risk: none (zero coupon). Interest rate risk: none (held to its one-year maturity — matures at par regardless of rate moves). FX risk: none (the forward fixes the conversion). Every risk is switched off by a clause in the stem → risk free.
questions.kr: 부도위험: 없음(무위험 발행자). 재투자위험: 없음(무이표). 금리위험: 없음(1년 만기까지 보유 — 금리와 무관하게 액면 상환). 환위험: 없음(선도로 고정). 지문의 조건 하나하나가 각 위험을 끔 → 무위험.

questions.stem: To set up the hedged HKD investment, the AUD-based investor would most likely:

choices.A: buy HKD forward, buy the HKD bond, sell AUD spot
choices.B: buy AUD spot, buy the HKD bond, sell AUD forward
choices.C: sell AUD spot, buy the HKD bond, buy AUD forward

questions.explanation: Trace the money: she holds AUD and needs HKD now → SELL AUD spot (= buy HKD spot). Buy the bond. At maturity she holds HKD and needs AUD → BUY AUD forward (= sell HKD forward). She cannot buy AUD spot — she already has AUD. This is the swap-funding structure: spot one way, forward back.
questions.kr: 돈의 흐름: 지금 AUD를 들고 HKD가 필요 → AUD 현물 '매도'(= HKD 현물 매수). 채권 매수. 만기엔 HKD를 들고 AUD가 필요 → AUD 선도 '매수'(= HKD 선도 매도). AUD는 이미 있으니 현물로 살 수 없음. 스왑 펀딩 구조: 현물로 가고 선도로 돌아옴.

questions.concept: Ex2 Q2 — what makes M–L more likely to hold
questions.stem: Australia runs a trade surplus with ε_X = 0.3 and ε_M = 0.6 (Marshall–Lerner fails). An appreciation of the AUD would be more likely to reduce the surplus if:

choices.B: ε_X decreases and the export share of trade falls
choices.C: ε_M decreases and the import share of trade rises

questions.explanation: 'More likely to reduce the surplus' = 'more likely that Marshall–Lerner holds' = HIGHER elasticities, always. Test each option against ω_X·ε_X + ω_M·(ε_M − 1): A raises both terms; B shrinks the export term; C makes the import term more negative AND gives it more weight — the exact opposite. Weight shifts only help if they shift toward the positive term.
questions.kr: '흑자를 줄일 가능성↑' = '마셜–러너 충족 가능성↑' = 탄력성이 '높아질' 때, 항상. ω_X·ε_X + ω_M·(ε_M − 1)에 대입: A는 두 항 모두 상승; B는 수출항 축소; C는 수입항을 더 음수로 만들고 가중치까지 키움 — 정반대. 가중치 이동은 양(+)인 항 쪽일 때만 도움.

questions.concept: Ex2 Q3 — identity: reduce a surplus
questions.stem: An appreciation of the AUD would reduce Australia's trade surplus if it led to an increase in Australian:

choices.B: private-sector investment
choices.C: budget surpluses

questions.explanation: X − M = (S − I) + (T − G). To REDUCE a surplus the right side must fall: S ↓, I ↑, or (T − G) ↓. Higher tax receipts and bigger budget surpluses both RAISE (T − G) → surplus grows. Higher investment lowers (S − I) → surplus shrinks. Sign every term before reading the options.
questions.kr: X − M = (S − I) + (T − G). 흑자를 '줄이려면' 우변 하락: S ↓, I ↑, (T − G) ↓. 세수 증가·재정흑자 확대는 (T − G)를 '올려' 흑자 확대. 투자 증가는 (S − I)를 낮춰 흑자 축소. 선지 읽기 전에 항마다 부호를 매긴다.

questions.concept: Ex2 Q6 — identity: surplus to zero
questions.stem: Capital controls that stop all financial flows force Australia's trade surplus to zero. The adjustment would most likely take the form of:

choices.B: a decrease in private investment
choices.C: an increase in the fiscal balance

questions.explanation: The surplus must FALL, so the right side of X − M = (S − I) + (T − G) must fall. Lower investment RAISES (S − I); a higher fiscal balance RAISES (T − G) — both would grow the surplus. Lower saving lowers (S − I) → surplus shrinks. Narrative: no credit to foreigners → export demand choked → income and profits fall → saving falls. 'Investment falling sounds like contraction' is intuition, not algebra.
questions.kr: 흑자가 '줄어야' 하므로 X − M = (S − I) + (T − G)의 우변이 하락해야. 투자 감소는 (S − I)를 '올리고', 재정수지 개선은 (T − G)를 '올림' — 둘 다 흑자 확대. 저축 감소가 (S − I)를 낮춰 흑자 축소. 서사: 외국에 신용 공급 불가 → 수출수요 위축 → 소득·이윤 하락 → 저축 하락. '투자 감소 = 수축 같다'는 직관이지 대수가 아님.

questions.stem: A three-month forward is traded on 18 October (T + 2 spot settlement). Its settlement date is most likely:

choices.B: 20 January
choices.C: 20 December

questions.explanation: Standard tenors count from the SPOT settlement date, not the trade date: trade 18 Oct → spot 20 Oct → three months → 20 Jan (rolled to the nearest good business day if it falls on a weekend/holiday).
questions.kr: 표준 만기는 거래일이 아니라 '현물 결제일'부터 계산: 18 Oct 거래 → 20 Oct 현물 → 3개월 → 20 Jan(주말·휴일이면 가장 가까운 영업일).

questions.stem: An FX swap is best described as:

choices.A: an exchange of fixed for floating interest payments in two currencies
choices.B: a simultaneous spot and forward transaction, typically used to roll a maturing forward
choices.C: an option to exchange currencies at a future date

questions.explanation: FX swap = offsetting spot trade + new forward, used to extend (roll) an expiring forward position; the roll produces a settlement-day cash flow equal to the mark-to-market. A is a currency (interest-rate) swap from derivatives; C is an FX option.
questions.kr: FX 스왑 = 상쇄 현물거래 + 새 선도, 만기 도래 선도 포지션을 연장(롤)하는 데 사용; 롤은 시가평가에 해당하는 결제일 현금흐름을 발생. A는 파생상품의 통화스왑, C는 FX 옵션.

questions.stem: A trader sold EUR 100m forward at USD/EUR 1.2000. Two days before settlement spot is 1.2100 and she rolls with an FX swap. On settlement day she most likely:

choices.B: pays USD 1,000,000
choices.C: has no cash flow, since the EUR amounts net

questions.explanation: She is short EUR at 1.2000 and must buy EUR spot at 1.2100 to deliver → sold low, bought high → loss: 100m × (1.2100 − 1.2000) = USD 1,000,000 PAID. The EUR nets to zero; the USD leg carries the loss. (At 1.1900 she would receive USD 1m.)
questions.kr: 1.2000에 EUR 숏인데 인도를 위해 1.2100에 현물 매수 → 싸게 팔고 비싸게 삼 → 손실: 100m × 0.01 = USD 1,000,000 '지급'. EUR는 상계, USD 쪽이 손실을 짊어짐. (1.1900이었으면 USD 1m 수취.)

questions.stem: A UK firm borrows USD, sells the USD for GBP spot, and simultaneously sells GBP forward against USD for 90 days. This structure most likely:

choices.A: leaves the firm with GBP for 90 days at a known all-in cost and no FX risk
choices.B: exposes the firm to GBP depreciation over the 90 days
choices.C: is cheaper than direct GBP borrowing by a wide margin

questions.explanation: Swap funding: the forward fixes the rate at which GBP is converted back to repay the USD loan → no FX risk and a known cost. Arbitrage keeps the all-in cost within a few basis points of direct GBP borrowing (covered interest parity) — not a wide margin.
questions.kr: 스왑 펀딩: 선도가 USD 대출 상환용 GBP→USD 환율을 고정 → 환위험 없음, 비용 확정. 차익거래가 총비용을 GBP 직접 차입과 몇 bp 이내로 유지(커버된 금리평형) — 큰 차이 아님.

questions.stem: When trade is initially balanced, the generalized Marshall–Lerner condition reduces to:

choices.B: ε_M > 1
choices.C: ε_X > ε_M

questions.explanation: With ω_X = ω_M = 0.5: 0.5ε_X + 0.5(ε_M − 1) > 0 → ε_X + ε_M > 1, the classic Marshall–Lerner condition. ε_M > 1 is the sufficient condition for import spending to fall on its own, not the balanced-trade reduction.
questions.kr: ω_X = ω_M = 0.5이면 0.5ε_X + 0.5(ε_M − 1) > 0 → ε_X + ε_M > 1, 고전적 마셜–러너 조건. ε_M > 1은 수입지출이 스스로 감소하는 충분조건이지 균형무역 축약형이 아님.

questions.concept: Deficit size and which elasticity matters
questions.stem: As a country's initial trade deficit becomes larger, the likelihood that a depreciation improves the trade balance depends most likely:

choices.A: more on the import elasticity and less on the export elasticity
choices.B: more on the export elasticity and less on the import elasticity
choices.C: equally on both elasticities regardless of the deficit

questions.explanation: A larger deficit means ω_M rises and ω_X falls, so the import term ω_M·(ε_M − 1) gets more weight and the export term less. With inelastic imports that term is negative, which is why large-deficit countries find depreciation less reliable.
questions.kr: 적자가 크면 ω_M↑·ω_X↓ → 수입항 ω_M·(ε_M − 1)의 비중이 커지고 수출항은 작아짐. 수입이 비탄력적이면 그 항이 음수라 대규모 적자국은 통화 약세의 효과를 덜 신뢰할 수 있음.

questions.stem: A depreciation is most likely to improve the trade balance when the country's traded goods are:

choices.B: luxuries with close substitutes sold in competitive markets
choices.C: a small share of consumer budgets

questions.explanation: Higher elasticities make Marshall–Lerner more likely to hold. Elasticity is higher for goods with good substitutes, in competitive markets, luxuries rather than necessities, and goods that are a large share of spending or input costs — the same four drivers as in Module 1.
questions.kr: 탄력성이 높을수록 마셜–러너 충족 가능성↑. 탄력성은 대체재가 많고, 경쟁시장이며, 필수재보다 사치재이고, 지출·투입비용에서 비중이 클 때 높음 — 모듈 1의 네 가지 결정요인과 동일.

questions.stem: The absorption approach to the trade balance differs from the elasticities approach most likely in that it:

choices.A: is microeconomic, focusing on expenditure switching between imports and exports
choices.B: is macroeconomic, focusing on income relative to domestic expenditure
choices.C: assumes exports are billed in foreign currency

questions.explanation: Absorption = macro: trade balance = income − absorption (= saving − investment); depreciation helps only if income rises relative to expenditure. Elasticities = micro: relative prices change and demand switches. Billing assumptions belong to the elasticities approach (exports in domestic currency).
questions.kr: 흡수접근 = 거시: 무역수지 = 소득 − 흡수(= 저축 − 투자); 통화 약세는 소득이 지출 대비 늘 때만 효과. 탄력성접근 = 미시: 상대가격 변화로 수요 전환. 표시통화 가정은 탄력성접근의 것(수출은 자국통화).

questions.stem: According to the absorption approach, a depreciation improves the trade balance of an economy with excess capacity most likely because:

choices.A: domestic prices rise until the stimulus is negated
choices.B: demand switches to domestic goods, output rises, and part of the extra income is saved
choices.C: households feel richer and spend more

questions.explanation: With slack, expenditure switching raises output and income; some of the extra income is saved, so income rises relative to expenditure → balance improves. Prices rising to negate the stimulus is the FULL-employment case; the wealth effect makes households feel POORER, not richer.
questions.kr: 유휴설비가 있으면 지출 전환이 산출·소득을 올리고 그 일부가 저축되어 소득이 지출 대비 증가 → 수지 개선. 물가 상승으로 자극이 상쇄되는 건 '완전고용' 경우; 부(富) 효과는 가계를 '더 가난하게' 느끼게 함.

questions.stem: According to the curriculum, a lasting correction of a chronic trade deficit most likely requires:

choices.B: fundamental changes in saving and expenditure behavior, such as an improved fiscal balance or higher real interest rates
choices.C: capital controls that block financial inflows

questions.explanation: Without excess capacity, depreciation's wealth effect is temporary. A durable fix needs saving to rise relative to investment — a better fiscal balance (S_g ↑) or higher real rates — the levers in CA = Sₚ + S_g − I. Capital controls force the balance to zero mechanically but through falling income and saving, not a sustainable adjustment.
questions.kr: 유휴설비가 없으면 통화 약세의 부 효과는 일시적. 지속적 교정은 저축이 투자 대비 늘어야 — 재정수지 개선(S_g↑) 또는 실질금리 상승 — CA = Sₚ + S_g − I의 레버. 자본통제는 소득·저축 하락을 통해 기계적으로 0으로 만들 뿐 지속가능한 조정이 아님.

questions.stem: For a depreciation to improve the trade balance, the absorption approach implies that, in addition to higher domestic saving:

choices.A: foreign assets must become relatively more attractive so the saving is channeled abroad
choices.B: domestic assets must become relatively more attractive to foreign investors
choices.C: the capital account need not change

questions.explanation: The BOP must balance: a trade surplus is matched by net acquisition of foreign assets. Domestic saving must be willingly invested in foreign financial assets, so asset prices adjust to make foreign assets relatively MORE attractive and domestic assets LESS attractive. The trade balance and financial account move together or not at all.
questions.kr: 국제수지는 균형: 무역흑자는 외국 자산의 순취득과 짝. 국내 저축이 외국 금융자산에 자발적으로 투자되어야 하므로 자산가격이 조정되어 외국 자산이 상대적으로 '더' 매력적, 국내 자산은 '덜' 매력적이 됨. 무역수지와 금융계정은 함께 움직이거나 아예 안 움직임.

questions.front: The FX hedging routine (missed 4 ways in Example 1): where the risk is, how to hedge, the setup sequence, the risk check, and the hedged-return formula
questions.back:
(1) Which currency am I LONG? (2) Risk = uncertainty over that currency's FUTURE SPOT rate — today's forward is a known price; next year's forward is irrelevant. (3) Hedge = SELL FORWARD the currency you are long (= buy domestic forward). (4) Setup = SELL domestic spot → invest foreign → BUY domestic forward (= swap funding).
Hedged, risk-free, zero-coupon, held to maturity → NO default, reinvestment, interest-rate, or FX risk → risk free.
Hedged return = (F/S) × (1 + i_foreign) − 1: AUD/HKD (0.1724/0.1714) × 1.022 − 1 = 2.8% (not the 2.2% HKD rate).

questions.front: Spot, forward, futures, FX swap, option — the distinguishing feature of each, and the swap roll cash flow
questions.back: SPOT: T + 2 (CAD vs USD T + 1); the quoted rate; a MINORITY of turnover. FORWARD: rate agreed today, settlement > T + 2; OTC, any size/date; tenors count from the spot date (18 Oct → 20 Oct → 20 Jan); liquidity falls with term and size. FUTURES: exchange (CME IMM), fixed amounts/dates, collateral + daily mark-to-market, minimal counterparty risk, less flexible. FX SWAP: simultaneous spot + forward; rolls an expiring forward; settlement cash flow = mark-to-market — sold EUR 100m fwd @1.2000, spot 1.1900 → EUR nets to zero, receive USD 1m (sold high, bought low). SWAP FUNDING: borrow USD → sell USD spot → sell GBP forward; no FX risk; ≈ domestic rate within bp. OPTION: premium for the right, not the obligation.

questions.front: Generalized Marshall–Lerner: formula, why the import term has −1, the four implications, Exhibit 1 numbers, and the J-curve
questions.back:
ω_X·ε_X + ω_M·(ε_M − 1) > 0; ω = shares of TOTAL trade; deficit → ω_M > ω_X. Exports billed in domestic currency → no price effect → term ≥ 0. Imports billed in foreign currency → price ↑ fights quantity ↓ → net (ε_M − 1); import spending falls only if ε_M > 1.
Implications: more elastic → more likely to improve; ε_M > 1 → definitely improves; bigger deficit → ε_M matters more; balanced trade → ε_X + ε_M > 1.
Exhibit 1: €↓10%, ε_X .75, ε_M .65, X 400 / M 600 → X +30, M +21 (spending UP), net +9; 0.4(.75) + 0.6(.65 − 1) = 0.09 ✓. Works best with substitutes, competitive markets, luxuries, large budget share.
J-curve: worse before better — pre-existing foreign-currency contracts + short-run elasticities fail while long-run ones hold.

questions.front: Absorption approach: the identity, excess capacity vs full employment, the wealth effect, the lasting fix — and the X − M = (S − I) + (T − G) sign rules (missed in M3, M6, M7×2)
questions.back:
Trade balance = income − absorption = saving − investment (macro; elasticities approach is micro expenditure-switching). EXCESS CAPACITY: output ↑, part saved → improves. FULL EMPLOYMENT: improves only if expenditure falls; else prices ↑ until stimulus negated → reverts. WEALTH EFFECT: weaker currency → real wealth ↓ → spend less, save more → improves → reverses as wealth rebuilt → TEMPORARY. Lasting fix: fiscal balance ↑ or real rates ↑. Capital account must move too: foreign assets relatively more attractive.
SIGNS: X − M = (S − I) + (T − G). Surplus SHRINKS (or deficit WIDENS) when S ↓, I ↑, or (T − G) ↓. Surplus GROWS (deficit shrinks) when S ↑, I ↓, or (T − G) ↑. Write it, sign each term, then read the stem — never from 'sounds like contraction'. Capital controls → trade balance forced to zero via falling income and saving.
